title: Anthropic open-sources the Model Context Protocol (MCP)
summary: Anthropic released MCP, an open standard for connecting AI assistants to data sources and tools through one common interface instead of custom integrations for each system.
whyItMatters: For AI PMs, standard connectors reduce integration cost and make tool-using assistants easier to build — but each connected tool also expands the permissions and security surface you must design for.

title: ‘Building effective agents’: workflows vs agents
summary: Anthropic published guidance distinguishing workflows (LLMs and tools orchestrated through predefined code paths) from agents (LLMs that dynamically direct their own process), recommending the simplest approach that works.
whyItMatters: A practical framing for scoping AI features: start with predictable workflows and add autonomy only when it clearly improves outcomes, because agents add cost, latency and failure modes.

title: Claude 3.5 models and ‘computer use’ in public beta
summary: Anthropic announced an upgraded Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Claude 3.5 Haiku and a beta capability for the model to operate a computer interface (viewing screens, moving a cursor, typing).
whyItMatters: Agents that act through user interfaces broaden what can be automated, but raise the stakes for confirmation steps, permission limits and prompt-injection defences.

source.title: Introducing computer use, a new Claude 3.5 Sonnet, and Claude 3.5 Haiku

title: Claude 3.7 Sonnet and Claude Code announced
summary: Anthropic introduced Claude 3.7 Sonnet, a model that can answer quickly or reason step by step for longer, along with Claude Code, an agentic coding tool.
whyItMatters: ‘Thinking time’ becomes a product choice: longer reasoning can raise quality on hard tasks at the cost of latency and tokens, so PMs must decide where it's worth it.

title: OpenAI introduces o1 reasoning models
summary: OpenAI described o1, a model series trained to spend more time reasoning before responding, with stronger results on complex maths, science and coding tasks.
whyItMatters: Reasoning models shift the cost–latency–quality trade-off: they can solve harder problems but are slower and costlier per request, which affects model routing decisions.

title: DeepSeek releases R1 open-weight reasoning model
summary: DeepSeek released DeepSeek-R1, an open-weight reasoning model, publishing the weights and a technical report.
whyItMatters: Capable open-weight models change build-vs-buy decisions: teams can self-host for privacy or cost at scale, but take on infrastructure, evaluation and safety work themselves.

title: Google announces the Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol
summary: Google announced A2A, an open protocol intended to let AI agents built by different vendors communicate and coordinate. It was later contributed to the Linux Foundation.
whyItMatters: Interoperability standards for agents may shape future platform strategy — but standards are still evolving, so avoid hard dependencies until adoption is clear.

title: OpenAI launches GPT-5
summary: OpenAI announced GPT-5, describing it as a unified system that decides when to respond quickly and when to reason longer, made available to ChatGPT users and developers.
whyItMatters: Automatic routing between fast and deep modes is becoming a built-in product pattern; PMs still need their own evals because general benchmarks don't guarantee quality on your tasks.

title: EU AI Act enters into force with phased obligations
summary: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, the AI Act, entered into force on 1 August 2024. Obligations apply in phases: prohibited practices from February 2025, general-purpose AI model obligations from August 2025, and most other rules from August 2026.
whyItMatters: Products serving EU users must classify AI use cases by risk and meet transparency and documentation duties. Involve legal early and check the current official timelines.

source.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act)
source.publisher: EUR-Lex, Official Journal of the EU

title: NIST publishes the Generative AI Profile of its AI RMF
summary: NIST released AI 600-1, a companion to the AI Risk Management Framework that describes risks unique to or worsened by generative AI and suggests actions to manage them.
whyItMatters: A voluntary, practical checklist for AI risk reviews — useful when building your own safety and evaluation processes.

title: India notifies the Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025
summary: The Government of India notified the DPDP Rules, 2025 under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, with most obligations phased in over roughly 18 months.
whyItMatters: Indian products handling personal data — including learner histories and AI prompts — need consent, security, breach-reporting and data-minimisation practices. Verify exact dates and obligations in the official text.

source.title: DPDP Rules, 2025 (PIB document)
